done.why: I went into the Royal Puzzle wanting to find whatever it hid, and I shoved sandstone blocks around without thinking ahead. The ladder block (the one facing west) ended up in the east column where nothing can push it again, and the other ladder faces east, so neither one can be got under the hole. There is no undo and pulling walls isn't allowed. Waiting and shouting did nothing, so I was sealed in with no way out.

about: This is the last stretch of an old underground empire: a ruin full of echoes from my earlier adventures. A silver-haired old man is testing me, and every gift I'm handed (a staff, a vial, a ring) seems to belong to him, as if I'm putting together his kit to earn a meeting with him. The world is about being generous to strangers, like hauling up a thief's chest or saying hello to a sailor. It's also about cleverness with time and place: a table that shows and visits other rooms, and a machine that sends you back to 776 GUE to take a ring before the jewels were locked up.

moments.note: 'Something that is not a tree is keeping very still' among the trees. A presence that won't show itself, nicely creepy.
Shouting up the cliff gets a chuckle, then the man hauls the chest up and leaves me stranded on the ledge.
While I wait on the ledge, every turn I hear the thief above: trying the lock, whistling, counting coins and starting over. The waiting felt alive.
He pulls me up and gives me a plain staff. Later his 'deep and sorrowful eyes' look borrowed, which hints at who he really is.
Examining the shadows calls up a hooded figure, and the stuck sword appears in my hand, glowing. I went down the cliff path and it faded away.
'hello sailor' worked and the sailor threw me a vial.
The lake shore text pushes very hard on 'leave everything on the shore.' Useful, but it felt like the room was nagging me.
The sparkling thing underwater keeps slipping out of my grasp, and the game never told me why.
Touching the Scenic Vista table sends me into the room it shows, including places from older adventures, and then snaps me back.
Room 8 with the grue repellent, reached through the table. The can's 'one moment of candour' description was a treat.

I touched the table at the bloody temple image and got sacrificed on the altar. Fair, since the table had warned me it was 'content to be looked at'. The death scene with the old man and the scattered belongings was memorable.
Time travel to 776 and everything I carried was gone. I worried for a moment, but found it all later in the Jewel Room.
Overhearing Lord Flathead dream up Flood Control Dam #3 through the door. Very funny.
Hiding the ring under the seat in the past and finding it there in the present was a great payoff.
The 3x3 grid diagrams for the puzzle are clear and made mapping in my head doable.
I pushed the ladder block east without knowing it couldn't be pushed back. Nothing warned me how permanent that was.
I explored nearly the whole grid and never found anything worth having in the puzzle. I couldn't tell what it was for.
'a wall of this kind is pushed, and pushed only.' That confirmed I was stuck for good.

wished: An undo, or some way out of a Royal Puzzle I had ruined
A warning when a push can't be reversed, especially the ladder wall
Some clue as to what the Royal Puzzle holds, so I could plan my pushes
Understanding why the shiny thing in the lake kept slipping away
Fighting or speaking to the hooded figure in the Land of Shadow instead of just backing off
Exploring the Aqueduct I could only look at from the balcony
Visiting the past museum more freely, past the locked iron door
Taking the waybread or the staff somewhere they actually mattered

lines.line: It has the look of an old friend who has followed you somewhere it would rather not have come.
lines.why: From the very first object it set a warm, wry tone, and it treats the lamp as a companion.

lines.line: The rock has the look of a thing that has been invited many times.
lines.why: A sly joke about every adventurer who has tried to pull the sword.

lines.line: tied to the trunk of one of the great trees with a knot that has thought about the matter
lines.why: Lovely small personification. The prose kept surprising me like this.

lines.line: The counting stops, and starts again from the beginning, by somebody who does not trust his own arithmetic.
lines.why: It made the wait on the ledge funny and full of character.

lines.line: with deep and sorrowful eyes, which sit oddly in a face like his, as though they had been borrowed from somebody graver
lines.why: A quiet hint that the thief is more than he seems.

lines.line: You cannot read the language, but the pictures read you: the flames are leaping up at a window, the statues stand either side of a way, and the old man is waiting.
lines.why: A hint that reads like a prophecy. It gave me the shape of the endgame.

lines.line: the small print is the Company's one moment of candour
lines.why: Classic Frobozz humour, and it also told me the can is good for one use only.

lines.line: the old man scatters what a visitor brings him, and it is lying where he left it, somewhere along the way in
lines.why: Death came with a rule I could understand, which made dying feel part of the world.

lines.line: We shall call it ... Flood Control Dam #3.
lines.why: Laugh-out-loud history overheard through a door.

lines.line: a wall of this kind is pushed, and pushed only.
lines.why: The line that told me I was stuck.

fun.why: The cliff and thief sequence, the sailor, the table teleports and the time-travel ring trick were all real pleasures. It lost a point because the puzzle softlock ended my run.

engagement.why: I wanted to see every room and kept going for over 200 turns. Busy waits like the one on the ledge held me, and the puzzle grid kept me mapping until I was walled in.

difficulty.why: Most puzzles were fair and well hinted: the lake shore, the table, the bronze plaque's 777 date. The lake hint even felt heavy-handed. The Royal Puzzle, though, let me lock myself in with no warning and no undo, and the lake bottom never told me why the shiny thing slipped away.

interestingness.why: Time travel to hide the ring, a table that visits places from older adventures, a thief who might be the old man, and grue repellent fetched from a room I could only reach through a picture. The ideas fit together and pay off.

prose.why: The prose is consistently wry and exact, and rich in small personifications (the knot, the invited rock, the borrowed eyes). The shore texts were the one place it got repetitive and over-explained.
